alignments.note: Conjunction.
Participle rendered as a temporal clause with its supplied subordinator and subject pronoun as rule 7 helpers, under rules 74 and 86.

εἰς τὸν οἶκον is rendered by the single English word home, so rule 94's count test makes the preposition and its governed word one unit. Rule 34's pleonastic arm is not available: rule 93 scopes it to a governed adverb, and where the governed word is a noun and the single English word is an adverb the adverbial force is what the preposition and the case contribute, exactly as ἐν τάχει → quickly stays one aligned unit on the noun wherever the preposition is written. Part of home answers to οἶκος's own lexeme, so rule 39's test keeps the unit aligned rather than noncompositional, and rule 93 heads it on the noun. The competing reading, leaving εἰς unrepresented because home reads as οἶκος's own gloss, is what rule 94's closing clause would require if the corpus spent a bare home on οἶκος; it does not, the corpus glossing that lexeme house.
No English determiner stands in home for the article to take (rule 23), and rule 93 keeps an article out of a compressed prepositional unit in any event.
Compound verb with its subject pronoun; the preverb συν- is realized by together, riding inside the unit under rule 106 and headed on the verb word.

review_notes: Corrected the εἰς τὸν οἶκον → home unit: the accepted alignment left εἰς unrepresented under rules 34 and 94, but rule 93 scopes the pleonastic arm to a governed adverb and denies it where the governed word is a noun and the single English word is an adverb. The preposition and the noun are now one aligned unit on home, headed on οἶκον, as ἐν τάχει → quickly is read at 1TI.3.14, REV.1.1, ROM.16.20 and LUK.18.8.
The article τόν is unrepresented either way, so the correction does not disturb it (rules 23 and 93).
All other units are unchanged; the two supplied possessives on τούς are the article's own under rule 20's second arm, no possessor standing in the Greek.
